ai_summary: Great Britain's wind generation currently stands at 5.7 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 2.9 GW, representing 28.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. While Scotland maintains an exceptionally clean local generation mix with a carbon intensity of just 4 gCO2/kWh, the wider GB-wide figure sits substantially higher at 180 gCO2/kWh. Transmission bottlenecks continue to impede the southward flow of renewable power, resulting in 2,244 MWh of Scottish generation curtailed so far today. Managing these network constraints has incurred an immediate cost of about £78,320. To compensate for this stranded zero-carbon energy, thermal generation elsewhere on the grid was brought online, burning an estimated 426,265 m3 of gas and releasing an additional 785 tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere. Annualising today's constraint expenditures indicates an estimated total yearly cost of £29 million. Recovered via balancing charges, this ongoing constraint expense increases electricity invoices across the UK by an estimated £0.10/MWh, underlining the urgent requirement for expanded cross-border transmission capacity to curb carbon emissions and reduce systemic balancing costs.
